📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

Sources indicate that the organization will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”.

Recent findings suggest that functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”.

Recent findings suggest that megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also declared it had debuted a criminal probe into the tech giant. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will enhancement this story if it responds.

After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hungary's fresh Prime Minister Peter Magyar arrived in Ukraine on Tuesday afternoon for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as well as with ethnic Hungarians living in the west of the country.

The meeting comes as both say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest — no doubt a welcome change for Kyiv after years of Viktor Orban obstructing funding for its self-defense against full-scaler Russian invasion.

Industry observers note that ukraine's Zelenskyy posted his thanks for the meeting with a photo on X, writing: "A visit that is sure to bring positive results. We already have agreements in the areas of politics, energy, and infrastructure. Thank you!".

Despite his softer approach, Magyar has remarked Hungary will not be sending arms to Kyiv while at the same time vowing, "we stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor.".

Magyar has insisted that the rights of tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians in the Transcarpathia — a region that was part of Austria-Hungary until the end of World War I and situated at the borders of Ukraine, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia — be resolved before Budapest can wholeheartedly back Ukraine and its possible accession to the European Union.

Relations deteriorated significantly over the matter in 2017, when Kyiv passed a law making Ukrainian the official language of all secondary education in Ukraine, something Budapest viewed as discriminatory toward ethnic Hungarians.

Last month, Ukrainian lawmakers passed legislation allowing ethnic minorities in the country expanded rights regarding the teaching and use of their native languages. The move was welcomed by Budapest and Hungary dropped its opposition to Brussels opening accession talks with Ukraine.

Magyar pitched this week's trip — the first to Transcarpathia by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015 — in April, after defeating Orban.

Before departing for Ukraine, the Hungarian leader noted: "I hope these talks will be successful. I think this is a historic day and a good opportunity to put Ukrainian-Hungarian relations on a newly introduced footing and to rebuild trust as we did with our other neighbors.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Democratic Republic of Congo military says it is searching for one of its aircraft, after rebels noted they had shot down a warplane in the east.
  • Sources indicate that the military said it had lost contact with a small Cessna 208 cargo plane on Sunday following "poor weather conditions".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Congolese rebels said they had targeted a warplane preparing to bomb the town of Minembwe.

The Democratic Republic of Congo military says it is searching for one of its aircraft, after rebels noted they had shot down a warplane in the east.

Sources indicate that the military said it had lost contact with a small Cessna 208 cargo plane on Sunday following "poor weather conditions". The fate of the plane and its crew remained uncertain, it added.

On the same day, the rebel Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) mentioned it had shot down a plane of the same type that was on a mission to bomb Minembwe in South Kivu province.

Four people were reportedly on board, including a Ugandan and a South African pilot, who is mentioned to have been captured alive.

On Tuesday, the FRN said the plane they had shot down was a Cessna 208, which had been "converted into a light attack aircraft" enabling it "to carry and launch precision-guided bombs and missiles".

Its wreckage now lies 10km (6 miles) from Minembwe, a rebel statement mentioned.

The BBC has not independently verified the rebel claim, or whether the aircraft reported missing by the DR Congo military is the same one the rebels say they shot down.

Uganda's military on Monday denied any involvement.

What's the fighting in DR Congo all about?

How former President Kabila became FRN rebel leader.

A statement attributed to army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba posted on X remarked: "UPDF had nothing to do with the aircraft that was shot down in Minembwe. We have penalized that firm.".

The statement did not identify the tech giant or explain what penalty had been imposed.

Gen Kainerugaba later posted that "no Ugandan is allowed to work for mercenary companies in [DR Congo]".

Uganda's denial followed the circulation of a video apparently showing a man being questioned beside the plane's wreckage.

It has been revealed that in the footage, the man identifies himself as Ugandan and claims he had been sent by the government. The BBC has not independently verified the video or established the man's identity.

He and the alleged South African pilot are remarked to be the only other survivors.

South African media outlet Mail & Guardian quoted an FRN spokesperson identifying the pilot as a South African and a "mercenary [who] has no link to the place that he was hired to destroy".

"Unfortunately, we have a multi-country conflict in the eastern DRC," deputy FRN spokesperson Oscar Balinda told the outlet.

In 2022, DR Congo's army blamed M23 rebels, who are now part of the FRN, of shooting down a UN helicopter in which eight people died. The rebels denied it.

The Congolese government has in the past used foreign mercenaries to fight the rebels.

In recent days, fighting between the FRN and the government has intensified with the rebel group accusing the government of targeting heavily populated areas.

The rebels control large areas of eastern DR Congo, including the major city of Goma, after major territorial advances last year.

Aid agencies say the violence is increasingly disrupting healthcare services.

Over the weekend, medical charity MÃ©decins Sans FrontiÃ¨res stated fighting in North Kivu had forced some of its teams to temporarily suspend outreach activities.

The fighting has also affected the response to the Ebola outbreak, with many health workers trapped, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The epicentre of the outbreak is in eastern DR Congo, which has been wracked by conflict for many decades, with some affected areas under rebel control.

Latest Update: Use this built-in Windows tool to find PC stability issues

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that an unstable PC can be a nightmare to diagnose.
  • In a recent development, introduced with Windows Vista back in 2008, Windows Reliability Monitor is a convenient way to check all of your computer's logged events.
  • Windows Reliability Monitor is an easy application to use, although accessing the program itself can be a little tricky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This tool is a great alternative to Event Viewer.

It has been revealed that an unstable PC can be a nightmare to diagnose. Figuring out what's causing a blue screen or a driver crash can take hours if you're digging through event logs and checking for faulty applications. Thankfully, Windows has a suite of troubleshooting programs built specifically to help users diagnose system issues. Most people know about Performance Monitor and Event Viewer, but arguably the best tool to start a troubleshooting session is the long-forgotten Windows Reliability Monitor.

In a recent development, introduced with Windows Vista back in 2008, Windows Reliability Monitor is a convenient way to check all of your computer's logged events. This includes crashed drivers, failed applications and other system health complications you might not otherwise notice. It even gives a stability score to help inexperienced users diagnose stability issues, although that score can be somewhat misleading. It's a great tool to use when your PC starts experiencing sudden stability issues that need further investigation.

Windows Reliability Monitor is an easy application to use, although accessing the program itself can be a little tricky. Every version of Windows can access the program by opening the Run box (Windows Key + R) and typing in:.

Industry observers note that if you are using Windows 8 or later, you can also find the Reliability Monitor by opening the Start menu and typing in "reliability." You should see "View reliability history" as an option. Click on it to bring up the Reliability Monitor. The Control Panel is a third way to access the Reliability Monitor, located under the "Security and Maintenance" subsection of the Security tab.

Sources indicate that the application itself is easy to understand. You'll see a grid of events that break down your system's stability based on event logs. Windows keeps track of hardware and application performance at all times, so if something goes wrong, it creates an event log entry that shows up here.

According to recent reports, clicking the blue "i" icons brings up information about your system that day, such as successful updates or software installations. Any days that experienced a critical software or hardware failure will have a red "x" icon next to them. Clicking the red icon will open the flagged events for further investigation. Days are also ranked with a stability score, indicating how long your PC has gone without complications. It's not the most reliable data point since you can easily inflate the score by not using your PC, but it can be a starting point when troubleshooting.

While Windows Reliability Monitor doesn't directly improve performance, it can help you find applications and faulty drivers that are causing performance problems. For example, if you experience frequent GPU crashes while running certain applications, those problems would be logged as events and appear in Reliability Monitor. Inspecting the event provides information on what caused the crash, when it occurred and what applications were running at the time. This can help diagnose whether it's a hardware or software issue, giving you a clear path to fix the error and improve your system's stability and overall performance.

If you are more focused on your system's performance, Windows offers the Performance Monitor tool to check your hardware's real-time usage. This is a better tool for diagnosing issues with a potentially faulty CPU, GPU, RAM, or network instability. Task Manager is also an invaluable tool for inspecting background applications that could be using your PC's resources.

More experienced Windows owners might wonder why they'd use the Reliability Monitor over the Event Viewer. For experienced PC users who want an exhaustive breakdown of each event log, the Event Viewer is unmatched. It offers significantly more information on each system event and has multiple ways to filter information to help pinpoint what's wrong.

Where Reliability Monitor shines is its simplicity. It gives a clean UI to see which events caused an issue, when they occurred and a rough outline of what happened. Event Viewer can help if you need details on the exact application or your PC's state during failure, yet that information is often overkill for the average Windows user. If you need more information on the issue, then we'd suggest swapping to Event Viewer to get a better idea of what's happening. For sudden performance or stability issues, it's much more convenient to use Reliability Monitor first.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress it seeks in the near-term for the federal government (see .pdf).

The list of so-called “funding anomalies” is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA’s Artemis program for a “higher rate of operations.”.

Sources indicate that the funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA’s Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China’s lunar ambitions are as expansive as those of NASA, and there is a very good chance the Asian country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there.

Industry observers note that fiscal year 2027 began on October 1 of this year, but the US Congress and White House have not agreed upon a budget. The government, including NASA, has been operating on a “continuing resolution” since that time. The existing continuing resolution remains in effect until December 11, by which time the parties need to agree to a final budget or another continuing resolution, or else the government will shut down.

It has been revealed that given the broad disagreement in funding priorities, it seems most likely that Congress will settle on another continuing resolution, punting a budget deal into the upcoming year and a new Democratic-led House and Senate. The release of the White House “anomalies” document signals to Congress what priorities the Trump administration wants to see addressed in a new continuing resolution that would be agreed to in the coming weeks, which the president would have to sign.

The budget plus-up for Artemis appears to be a significant win for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, who arrived at the space agency 11 months ago, after the White House had already put together its “President’s Budget request” for the fiscal year 2027 process. This is the first time he has had a chance to work with the Trump administration on budget priorities, and in doing so has convinced officials that NASA deserves more funding in its race back to the Moon.

Sources indicate that as part of the description for the funding, the document indicates that NASA is seeking additional funding for Artemis without stripping away money for existing programs in other areas such as science. “Additional topline is needed to support this effort without jeopardizing other priorities outlined in the National Space Policy,” the White House document states.

It has been revealed that the key challenge for NASA in the next two years, as part of its return to the Moon, is working with SpaceX and Blue Origin to finalize development of their lunar landers—a key untested piece of the mission initiative that carries astronauts down from lunar orbit to the Moon’s surface, provides a temporary habitat there, and then returns the crew members to lunar orbit. The space agency has been seeking to help both companies work through supply chain and test complications.

It has been revealed that NASA also has been working to increase its own in-house technical capabilities in order to help Axiom Space develop a lunar space suit and assist private companies developing a panoply of smaller landers and lunar hardware to provide power, communications, and other services as part of the agency’s Moon Base initiative. These companies all face serious supply chain issues for key hardware components.

Sources indicate that “Language is needed to provide an additional $2 billion to meet the schedule for Artemis acceleration activities to include supply chain acceleration via in-house manufacturing and modernization of NASA’s in-house capabilities in areas such as suits, thrusters, SLS-related hardware, habitats, and safety systems for astronauts,” the White House document states. “Without this funding, activities would be delayed, missing the required operational need date.”.

Notably, the document also includes the following language: “NASA needs to build and retain the ability to manufacture complex low-rate components and major assemblies.” This suggests the White House wants NASA to have the infrastructure to manufacture specialized components when commercial suppliers cannot deliver them sufficiently quickly or reliably.

Importantly, the language in the White House funding request appears deliberately broad, giving Isaacman substantial flexibility to identify the most pressing bottlenecks in the Artemis program and direct resources toward addressing them quickly.

The explosion ripped through one of the city's central squares.

A car bomb has exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring at least 23 people.

The explosive device was detonated in front of the offices of the regional government, in the city centre, damaging several buildings.

No group has so far admitted carrying out the attack - the latest in a series using explosives to target official buildings and security forces' headquarters.

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed "narcoterrorism", but gave no details. Armed criminal groups have recently stepped up attacks in what appears to be retaliation for an offensive ordered against them by De la Espriella.

Writing on social media, the president said that his government would "bluntly and forcefully" respond, external to "every drop of Colombian blood spilled".

"There will be no impunity and no retreat," he added.

It is the latest in a series of attacks targeting official buildings and security forces' headquarters.

Three weeks ago, three adults and a baby were killed in a car bomb attack near army barracks in Tolima province.

And earlier on Monday, drones dropped explosives on the police headquarters in the northern city of CÃºcuta.

The car bomb in Villavicencio went off on Monday evening - the eve of the 10th anniversary of the signing of a peace deal between the government and left-wing rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), Colombia's largest guerrilla group.

Following the signing of the deal, thousands of left-wing rebel fighters laid down their arms.

However, a significant number of Farc members, who did not agree with the deal, refused to disarm and joined dissident groups instead.

While forced displacement, child recruitment and the numbers of attacks on security forces dropped in the aftermath of the deal, there has been an upsurge in recent years driven by dissident Farc factions and criminal groups fighting for control of drug trafficking, illegal mining and extortion rackets.

Colombia's first left-wing president, who was in power from August 2022 to August 2026, tried to negotiate with these armed groups as part of what he called his "total peace" strategy.

However, the talks stalled and collapsed with several of the criminal groups violating ceasefires they had agreed to observe.

De la Espriella was elected on a promise to crack down on "narcoterrorism" and has been scathing about his predecessor's approach.

He has also been critical of the 2016 agreement, calling it a "false peace".

In a post on X, uploaded shortly before news of the car bomb in Villavicencio spread, he referred to the peace deal as a "mess", describing it as a "waste of public resources" and the "cause behind Colombia's ruin".

Former President Juan Manuel Santos and Rodrigo LondoÃ±o - the two men who signed the peace deal on behalf of the Colombian government and the Farc respectively - defended it in an interview with BBC Mundo ahead of the anniversary.

Santos stated that De la Espriella was "totally wrong" to call it a "false peace".

"He wants to use, or has bought into that cynical and mistaken theory that the violence we see today is the result of the peace deal, when the exact opposite is the case," Santos mentioned, arguing that the problem lies with the lack of implementation of the agreement.

Industry News: Researchers find 3.6 billion usernames, passwords and documents in unsecured databases

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The scale of the exposed data underscores how key it is to take steps to stay safe online.
  • In a recent development, security researchers have unearthed two unsecured databases containing more than 3.6 billion records, including usernames, passwords, documents and national identity numbers.
  • According to recent reports, he said the database contains hundreds of millions of email accounts, north of 100 million social media accounts and tens of millions of ecommerce accounts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The scale of the exposed data underscores how key it is to take steps to stay safe online.

In a recent development, security researchers have unearthed two unsecured databases containing more than 3.6 billion records, including usernames, passwords, documents and national identity numbers. Wired reported that Black Hills Information Security researcher Jeremiah Fowler found one of the databases, which contains roughly 2 billion login credentials. Fowler mentioned they were "associated with virtually every type of online service imaginable.".

According to recent reports, he said the database contains hundreds of millions of email accounts, north of 100 million social media accounts and tens of millions of ecommerce accounts. It's estimated to include more than 114 million accounts linked to Google services, 88 million Facebook accounts, nearly 33 million X accounts, almost 42 million Roblox accounts and 36.6 million Amazon accounts, though Fowler indicated there may be some overlap between services and/or individual customers.

It has been revealed that the database is noted to feature thousands of folders with plaintext credentials and account details. Dozens of countries were specified in the folder names, including the US, UK, France and Germany. There were also about 400,000 documents that "appeared to come from more advanced malware that created separate folders for individual victims," according to Fowler.

It has been revealed that the other database reportedly contains north of 1.6 billion documents, primarily relating to people and businesses in China. It's said to include at least 840 million distinct national ID numbers, 300 million phone numbers, approximately 11 million student enrollment records (many of which were for minors) and 7.8 million business registrations.

Sources indicate that greg Pollock, security manufacturer UpGuard's director of research, found the database on the public internet on what appeared to be a gray market framework. Pollock told Wired the database was updated as recently as a week before he spotted it in October.

Sources indicate that both databases — which have been removed from where the researchers found them — collated information from multiple sources, according to the report. The larger database is noted to include data procured by infostealer malware that can harvest all login credentials from a single device, along with information obtained from elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that as for the China-focused database, "the data comes from sources controlled by entirely separate authorities: ID registration (the Ministry of Public Security), payment app data (Ant Group, a private company), student enrollment (the education system) and business registration (market regulators)," Pollock wrote in a blog post. "No single lawful holder could legally possess all of them. The underlying records almost certainly originated in real government, telecom and corporate systems. What this server represents is the assembly of that stolen material into a working product.".

Industry observers note that at this point, it's reasonable to assume that some of your private data is out there. Data breaches, unfortunately, happen all the time — I've been notified about at least three that have impacted me and my information in the last month. The proliferation of AI is making it easier for attackers to find system vulnerabilities, gain access to a organization's or organization's servers and make off with data. AI can help them collate disparate information into databases such as these too.

Still, there are measures you can take to help protect yourself and your data. Having strong, unique passwords for every single service you use is absolutely vital. A password manager can help you juggle all of those. Passkeys, multi-factor authentication and a good VPN are very useful too. Being more judicious about what information you share and with which services should stand you in better stead, as will being vigilant for social engineering and phishing attacks. Data removal services can come in handy as well.

AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.

Now, the organization has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s presently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.

In a recent development, michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.

“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano mentioned. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.

It has been revealed that the team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading releases like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.

Recent findings suggest that the startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a fresh level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.

Right now, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the firm intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.

Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.

According to recent reports, supertake’s owners’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s at the moment an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.

For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.

Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.

“We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he indicates. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”.

“I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he says.

Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.

“We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being noted, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.

To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team notes it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.

In a recent development, “We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” says Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”.

Access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders stated they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.

Mignano, meanwhile, claims he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.

According to recent reports, with the latest funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. Mignano and Murr are in New York, while Peterson is in the Austin area but commutes to New York at times. The team notes it hopes to figure out a hybrid work model as it grows.

Anthropic introduces Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship.
  • The latter is the more interesting part of this latest set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now.
  • According to recent reports, the launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI organization announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this latest set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

According to recent reports, the launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

In a recent development, “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”.

Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

It has been revealed that the new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing problems such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

According to recent reports, claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the manufacturer’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

Sources indicate that because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

Anthropic indicates teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.

Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The partnership is pulling human safety drivers from its Lucid Gravity SUVs ahead of an early 2027 commercial debut.﻿.

The partnership is pulling human safety drivers from its Lucid Gravity SUVs ahead of an early 2027 commercial debut.﻿.

Sources indicate that uber’s high-stakes robotaxi bet is officially ditching its human safety net. Nuro, Lucid, and Uber are starting fully driverless public road testing in the San Francisco Bay Area, with employee-only rides launching shortly after.

In a recent development, first confirmed in July 2025, this three-way alliance represents Uber’s aggressive comeback in autonomous ride-hailing, after having abandoned its own troubled in-house efforts years ago. By pulling human safety operators from behind the wheel of Lucid Gravity SUVs, the companies say they are clearing a critical hurdle toward a public launch. That debut is now slated for early 2027, marking a slight slip from the partnership’s original late-2026 target. When it finally goes live, it will pit Uber directly against entrenched rivals like Waymo and Zoox on their home turf.

Driverless testing kicks off across four South Bay cities—Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos, and Sunnyvale—before expanding across the broader Bay Area next year. To fuel this push, Lucid has delivered more than 100 upgraded Gravity SUVs, up from the 75 engineering vehicles on the road earlier this year.

It has been revealed that the automaker began building pre-production models in October to clear regulatory safety approvals, and it intends to start manufacturing the actual commercial fleet in the coming weeks. Each SUV is powered by Nuro’s Level 4 “Nuro Driver” system, pairing cameras, solid-state lidar, and radar with a roof-mounted LED “halo” that flashes a rider’s initials and pickup status.

It has been revealed that removing the human backup comes after nearly a year of round-the-clock supervised testing in the Bay Area and Houston. Before letting the cars loose on public streets alone, Nuro put the software through grueling, high-risk edge cases on a closed track in Las Vegas to prove it could handle the unpredictable chaos of real-world driving.

Looking further ahead, Uber has committed to buying at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles—including the automaker’s upcoming midsize model—over the coming years as it races to scale a global autonomous fleet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary.

In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.

"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions.

In the diary, written from 1992 to 2024, he also expresses regret over his 2018 visit to Chile, when he was criticised for defending a bishop who was accused of covering up sexual abuse committed by a priest.

Francis, who led the Catholic Church for 12 years until his death in 2025, later apologised and summoned the country's bishops to Rome, where they all offered to resign.

"Devastated because of the situation in Chile," Francis wrote in a 2021 entry.

"It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious.".

Of his encounters, which Francis interpreted as meetings with the devil, he mentioned he could not forget the devil's "menacing" eyes.

"He looked at me with flaming eyes... more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire," he wrote of his second vision that he said happened inside a Carmelite chapel while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires.

He said the devil's presence intruded on his journeys, including during the visit to Chile amid the clerical sexual abuse scandal, and a meeting a few days after he had returned to Rome.

"I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".

The collection of diaries was edited by a longtime friend of Francis.

The late pope also revealed that while getting ready to go to sleep in June 2018, he "saw the gates of hell".

"I watched a little, and it terrified me," he remarked, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".

"It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.

Cardinal Victor Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and friend of Francis, edited the diaries, which are the first by a pope to be released to the public since the 1960s.

Pope Francis was elected pope in 2013 and died aged 88 in April 2025.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Figma engineer is suing the design software manufacturer and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.

It has been revealed that the lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Fresh York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the company’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.

“Figma was my dream tech giant for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”.

It has been revealed that park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.

Recent findings suggest that when reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma stated, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”.

Park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the organization would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”.

Industry observers note that park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.

Sources indicate that park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.

Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.

It has been revealed that the lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It indicates the organization’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.

In a recent development, in March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching strategy, which she completed in late 2023.

Industry observers note that changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.

Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.

In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.

Industry observers note that on her latest team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.

It has been revealed that the incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly said Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.

A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had remarked. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.

During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly said she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”.

According to recent reports, the manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.

“Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit said.

According to recent reports, park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.

Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.

It has been revealed that in early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”.

Park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.

Industry observers note that park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time she returned to work. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.

“It’s really scary for me,” she noted about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”.

This piece was updated to clarify when Park said Figma implemented the recommendations from her medical professionals.

#173123. Tech Report: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in Upcoming York from 2027

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (505 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in Upcoming York from 2027

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year.
  • Recent findings suggest that “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car.
  • Sources indicate that in the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year.

Recent findings suggest that “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor noted.

Sources indicate that in the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee.

We end users might not like having to open our wallets each month, but the capital markets sure do, and car companies love making the capital markets happy. Which is why there has been such a push toward connected vehicles. Remote start and predictive maintenance alerts are nice, but your regular payments to the car firm—plus any data of yours it can sell—is the goal.

Some automakers have gone even further. Infamously, BMW and its heated seats. Like the McDonalds coffee lawsuit, it’s a fact half-remembered; BMW North America never tried such a thing, just in countries like South Korea and the UK, and in 2023 BMW’s board mentioned that subscriptions would only be for software-related features from then on.

Upcoming York’s press release mentions heated seats but also calls out a number of other modern tech features: “enhanced navigation, hands-free driving and entertainment options that do not present an ongoing expense for dealers and manufacturers.”.

But the way the actual law is written appears to leave a rather large loophole, at least to these eyes.

S.9348A/A.10411A prohibits motor vehicle manufacturers, dealers or third-party service providers from adding subscription services or charging post-purchase fees for any motor vehicle feature that uses pre-installed components or hardware that do not have an ongoing cost. As vehicles become more advanced, the new law aims to establish clear rules preventing exploitative practices and prevent post-purchase fees as a future automotive business model.

According to recent reports, A heated seat might not have “an ongoing cost,” but the maps and databases that enable “enhanced navigation” and “hands-free driving” systems definitely do, as these need to be constantly updated. A regular cadence of software updates also generates an ongoing cost to an OEM, arguably. And car companies pay for plenty of lawyers who really love to argue.

And so, while experiments like BMW’s seat heater subscription won’t be allowed in the state, the upcoming rule might still allow for plenty of ongoing fees for services like OnStar or Mercedes’ Drive Assist Pro system we tested recently.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bambu cut a few corners — and motors — to reach that price.

Bambu cut a few corners — and motors — to reach that price.

It has been revealed that if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Three weeks ago, Bambu Lab introduced the state of the art in home printing tech at $2,499 — now, you can get many of its fancy new features for less than half the price.

Like that bigger H3C, the newly introduced $1,149 Bambu P3C can also swap between materials on the fly, mix different colors to produce much of the rainbow, mix soft and hard materials, even mix different sizes of nozzle and different diameters of filament so you can switch between high speed and fine detail in a single print.

But Bambu cut more corners than I expected to hit the lower $1,149 / £999 / €1,149 launch price today, and I think they made more of a tinkerer’s 3D printer than one suited for either beginners or pros.

Some of the changes were completely expected, like its smaller 256 x 256 x 260mm print area (much like Bambu’s other P-series printers), and that it supports seven automatically swapping tools instead of nine. (Seven is still quite a lot when affordable toolchangers like the $849 Snapmaker U1 typically offer just four.).

In a recent development, but unlike the H3C, the P3C doesn’t come fully loaded, and it doesn’t load itself. While it has slots for seven rolls of filament and up to seven independent tools (including thicker-than-usual 2.85mm filament, or pens, cutting blades, and debossing and foil transfer tools if you want it to double as a Cricut), it only comes with five 0.4mm print nozzles by default.

And while five is still one more color than you’d get with an $800 Bambu P2S Combo, the 3D printer I’d buy for myself, the Bambu P3C’s automated material system (AMS) is the first Bambu has shipped without any motors to automatically load your filament.

Recent findings suggest that don’t get me wrong: You can still keep five colors of filament ready to go at a moment’s notice, one more than the P2S, by keeping them loaded into the P3C’s five independent nozzles. You can also buy and fairly easily install two more printheads as well, though they cost up to $100 each.

But loading those nozzles is a slow and surprisingly manual process where you have to shove a string of filament down a tube, quite a long distance by hand, after waiting for the machine to preheat each one, and it feels like a step backwards after years using the earlier motorized versions of Bambu’s AMS. Then again, the P3C doesn’t have to spend time and filament purging between colors like the P2S does.

Recent findings suggest that I expect many 3D printing enthusiasts will see $1,149 for the Bambu P3C as a pretty good deal, assuming they haven’t written off the manufacturer’s gadgets after Bambu’s open source snafus. Even five nozzles is enough to load all five rolls of Bambu’s “PLA Palette” cyan, magenta, yellow, black, and white (CMYKW) filaments for color mixing to produce beautiful creations like the company’s new hummingbird test print, which came out almost flawlessly on my first try.

According to recent reports, but you should know that color mixing isn’t necessarily a foolproof way to produce some colors, like the brown tree branch that’s supposed to be the hummingbird’s perch, and I’m not looking forward to manually pulling and pushing a roll of brown filament to change that. Bambu indicates I should probably try a feature called “mixed color sublayer” for better results, and I also suppose I could daisy-chain a normal motorized AMS to one of the P3C’s printheads, as that is a supported workflow. But that’s why I’m suggesting we’re in tinkerer territory.

I asked Bambu about the decision to not include filament-loading motors in the P3C’s AMS system, and here’s part of the statement I got back from spokesperson Karlie Hou: “The AMS 3P’s design deliberately omits the auto‑loading feature as part of the effort to offer premium multi‑head performance at roughly half the price of the flagship H3C system, allowing a far broader audience — hobbyists, small studios, and educational institutions — to enjoy premium multi‑head, multi‑color printing experience.”.

Recent findings suggest that the company says it should take around five minutes to manually reload five nozzles. “In the next [software] enhancement, we aim to shrink the total hands‑on time for loading five spools to under one minute,” the company writes, though that seems like a tall order.

Industry observers note that maybe I’ll put the P3C to a year-long test like I did with the P2S, and see how often I actually need something CMYKW can’t do for me, and whether the filament stays dry when left in the printheads for a long time. The question is: What printers should I test against? Are there any upcoming ones I should wait for?

A funeral was held earlier in southern Gaza for three Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike.

At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.

It has been revealed that naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.

The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.

According to recent reports, three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.

Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, stated two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.

The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.

Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.

Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.

The Israeli military noted Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".

It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".

Gaza's interior ministry stated Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "key achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".

Gaza's health ministry warned that there was a rapid rise in cases of meningitis in October.

Sources indicate that violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.

At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.

The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.

The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.

On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.

Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it stated.

Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,740 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry states.

Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says.

Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line.

UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza.

Wireless Android Auto has a phone battery draining problem, but you can fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A vent mount and a few settings changes are enough to block the drain.
  • An hour of wireless Android Auto can sap up to 16 percent of a phone's battery when you've got everything turned on.
  • After all, wireless Android Auto uses both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and both stay switched on for your entire drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A vent mount and a few settings changes are enough to block the drain.

An hour of wireless Android Auto can sap up to 16 percent of a phone's battery when you've got everything turned on. Navigation, as well as music, can heat your phone up, which isn't great news since most people will charge their phones during the drive. That charging adds even more heat, and a phone that gets too hot may slow down its own charging to protect the battery.

After all, wireless Android Auto uses both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and both stay switched on for your entire drive. Long stints using navigation and other demanding apps while charging have been acknowledged as some of the reasons a Pixel can overheat. Once it's too hot, the phone might reduce processor performance or partly switch off mobile data, including 5G.

Recent findings suggest that but there are a few things you can do to help mitigate battery drain and heat, like turning off 5G or using offline maps. And for longer drives, you can plug the phone in to maintain its charge and keep it out of direct sunlight, ideally near an air-conditioning vent to help it stay cool.

Industry observers note that google has said that managing heat was one of the main reasons it capped the Pixel 10 and Pixel 10 Pro at 15W wireless charging, because a wireless pad can add even more thermal energy. A phone that's sitting on a pad, which itself is probably on a sunny dashboard while running navigation, can build up heat from several sources at once, potentially slowing charging.

Sources indicate that google's advice to prevent a Pixel from overheating is to keep it out of direct sunlight and away from hot vehicles and poorly ventilated spots. One way to reduce heat is to use a vent mount while the vent is blowing cold air instead of a dashboard cradle in full sun. Even moving the phone somewhere with ample airflow while not relying on charging during wireless Android Auto use can help substantially.

A USB connection can generally keep your phone cooler and charge it more effectively than wireless Android Auto on a wireless charging mount. But car ports vary, and some vehicle USB ports could be too slow to stop the battery from draining, depending on automaker specifications. If you want to switch to a wired connection, Android Auto has a developer menu you can access in seconds. While Google removed the wireless Android Auto switch from the app's regular settings in version 8.7, it remains available in the hidden developer settings, so you can turn wireless Android Auto off and connect the phone with a USB cable.

Switching from 5G to LTE appears to make the biggest difference to battery life, because some networks force a phone to maintain an LTE connection alongside 5G, which increases power consumption. LTE is thankfully fast enough for navigation and music. To improve your Samsung Galaxy's battery performance, go to Settings > Connections > Mobile networks > Network mode and select LTE preferred. On other phones, look for Network mode or Preferred network type. Turning off 3D buildings in Google Maps can also help to reduce heat. With your car parked, open Google Maps on the car's screen, go into its Settings and turn off 3D buildings.

Google Maps can save a map of your route before you leave, reducing mobile data use and strain on the device. Tap your profile picture, then Offline maps > Select your own map, adjust the area to cover your route and tap Download. Offline maps can't reroute around live traffic or latest road challenges as they develop, so going offline is generally best saved for long, predictable drives such as those on a highway or where you're familiar with the roads.

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning help apps get better location information, too. You can switch both off under Settings > Location > Location services, removing another background job. Wireless Android Auto still needs Wi-Fi and Bluetooth turned on, though. To stop it launching when you don't want it to, you can toggle off the setting Start Android Auto while locked, which can prevent it from starting while your phone is locked. This doesn't stop calls from connecting over Bluetooth.

In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned.

During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Industry observers note that early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.

Huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board said in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement.

The Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.

Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Saurav Das remarked that he was supposed to deliver a series of lectures in the UK.

One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.

Saurav Das noted he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.

In an interview with the BBC, Das stated there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on complications that matter to young people.

The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident highlighted the government was "scared".

"They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them.".

By not allowing him to travel, he remarked the government had lowered India's stature in the world.

Industry observers note that "It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he noted. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light.

"It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government.".

Saurav Das (L) speaking following the resignation of India's education minister in July.

Das said he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement.

Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country.".

On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".

Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.

In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .

In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.

The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

Das insisted the CJP would continue protesting, but it did not want to be a political party "as of today".

"It's a long haul. We are not here for a short time. We are looking at India in the next 10 to 20 years. How do we develop India into a better country? That is the vision that we want to carry forward.".

Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.

There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.

In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.

She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, jensen Huang’s comeback as Nvidia’s CEO is understandably making waves, leaving people wondering about the longer-term implications of his quick reinstatement and the U.S. government’s active role in his return. But there was another development yesterday that could also matter for Nvidia down the road: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart‘s tech and its team for a reported $7.5 billion.

The broader industry seems to agree that Decart’s tech for optimizing AI models to run on non-Nvidia chips is worth several billion dollars. Anthropic reportedly tried to acquire the startup in the same ballpark, and Nvidia, which invested in the startup’s $300 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation, was also rumored as a prospective buyer.

Amazon was ultimately the one to pull the trigger and bring on board Decart’s co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev and their team, but the manufacturer is not interested in the world models they had been working on. At the heart of the deal is the startup’s tech that helps AI models run better on all kinds of chips.

By incorporating the startup’s Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), Amazon is now hoping to extract more performance out of its Trainium chips, as the company tries to turn AWS into a $1 trillion revenue business.

Sources indicate that in its announcement, Amazon said it has worked with Decart since 2025 to optimize the Trainium chips. This deal is ostensibly aimed at accelerating that work, which could eventually result in the manufacturer offering its Trainium-based data centers, which Anthropic already uses, to more customers. Amazon has already been working to make Trainium easier to switch to.

Industry observers note that one way Nvidia managed to leapfrog its competitors was by spending $6.9 billion to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox, which eventually grew to become a core piece of its international manufacturing strategy. Amazon could well be following a similar path.

Sources indicate that annapurna Labs makes for a more interesting parallel than Mellanox, however, as the latter formed the basis of Amazon’s custom chip-designing unit following its 2015 acquisition. Add Intel into the mix, and this becomes a broader story. “Most of the hardware powering the AI wave was built in Israel. Annapurna; Mellanox; Habana Labs; etc…,” VC Eric Reiner observed on X a few months ago.

In an email to TechCrunch, Eze Vidra, co-founder and managing partner at Remagine Ventures, said the deal is “a strong signal for the Israeli deep-tech ecosystem, showing that specialized local talent continues to attract major global players.”.

Industry observers note that amazon still has a ways to go before it can make a dent in Nvidia’s near-monopoly on AI chips, but the deal could help the e-commerce giant speed up its efforts. Dean Meyer, a partner at Sequoia who co-led the firm’s seed investment into Decart, noted on X that the deal “will be looked back on as one of the most strategically important acquisitions in many, many years.”.

A year ago, Wyze introduced a $35 security camera that stuck to the inside of a window so you could keep an eye on what was happening outside your home without a complicated installation. Today the company announced its new Window Bird Cam, which expands on that idea by pairing a similar window-mounted camera with a feeder that attaches to the outside of the glass. Alongside the kit, Wyze is also launching a new subscription service called Bird Watch, which adds identification capabilities and features that will benefit busy yards.

In a recent development, the Wyze Window Bird Cam is available today through the company’s online store for $69.98 and includes the outdoor feeder with suction cups for mounting, a small tray for holding seeds, and a cover for protection from the elements. Wyze is also selling an optional $14.98 accessory called the Window Bird Cam Perch that gives birds a ”natural landing spot right in the camera’s portrait sweet spot,“ plus a fruit fork, suet holder, and a jelly cup to attract more visitors.

By installing inside your home and plugging into a USB power source (using an included 10-foot cable) the Bird Cam doesn’t need a battery, doesn’t need to be weatherproof, and will be well in range of your Wi-Fi network. Instead of the wide-angle view offered by most security cameras, the lens on the Bird Cam is designed to focus at a distance of 4 to 8 inches so birds look crisp while the rest of your yard is softly blurred.

Out of the box, the Bird Cam will detect motion and provide instant bird arrival notifications while 30fps video is recorded locally to a microSD card up to 512GB. You can also watch and share a livestream from the camera through a mobile device. The arrival notifications do have a five-minute cooldown so if you want to ensure you don’t miss any visitors, you’ll need to upgrade to Bird Watch for $6.99 per month, or $69.99 per year. The subscription adds species identification with a confidence score and access to an interactive bird wiki, full-length videos of bird visits stored in the cloud for 60 days, and no cooldown period between notifications.

Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co
